newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan stocks end up but off highs on late selling.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan stocks end up but off highs on late selling.

text.p: Taiwan share prices finished up but off their early highs on Saturday as jitters over domestic political problems triggered waves of late selling, brokers said.
The weighted index closed 40.82 points or 0.50 percent higher at 8,274.19 points, down from an intra-day high of 8,359.91. Turnover was a heavy T$116 billion in the abbreviated Saturday session.
Rumours that government-related funds had entered to support the market inspired early buying, but brokers said investors were cautious ahead of next week's cabinet reshuffle.

The administration, which has faced intense criticism over a spate of violent crime, was expected to announce a reshuffle next week. Three cabinet members have tendered their resignations so far, shocking the public as well as the ruling Nationalist Party.
"The cabinet reshuffle will be the market focus next week," said George Hou, a fund manager of Jardine Fleming.

"If the reshuffle does not meet the public expectations, we can expect more selling by disappointed investors," Hou said. "The market will stay in a consolidation as long as the political situation remains unclear," he added.
Brokers noted that recent buying interest was concentrated on electronic shares.
"There is a general optimism toward the electronic sector at the moment. But the problem is that not every electronic company can generate high profits," Jardine Fleming's Hou said.
The sector gained 3.20 percent, with Taiwan Semiconductor up T$5 or 4.57 percent to T$114.5.
A trading range of 8,000-8,500 was expected next week, brokers said.
